```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# Load required R packages
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(reticulate)

# Only try to load JuliaCall if needed
if (!requireNamespace("JuliaCall", quietly = TRUE)) {
  message("JuliaCall not available. Julia visualization will not work.")
  julia_available <- FALSE
} else {
  library(JuliaCall)
  julia_available <- TRUE
  
  # Try to initialize Julia
  tryCatch({
    julia_setup(verbose = FALSE)
    message("Julia initialized successfully")
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Julia initialization failed: ", e$message)
    julia_available <- FALSE
  })
}

# Clean data for plotting
data(penguins)
penguins_clean <- penguins %>% 
  drop_na(bill_depth_mm, body_mass_g, species)

# Save data for Julia (only if Julia is available)
if (exists("julia_available") && julia_available) {
  write.csv(penguins_clean, "penguins_clean.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}

# Prepare data for Python
py_penguins <- penguins_clean %>%
  mutate(species = as.character(species)) %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

## R Visualization

```{r r-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
# Create scatter plot with R
ggplot(penguins_clean, aes(x = body_mass_g, y = bill_depth_mm, color = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Adelie" = "darkorange", "Chinstrap" = "purple", "Gentoo" = "#008080")) +
  labs(
    title = "Bill Depth vs Body Mass by Penguin Species (R)",
    x = "Body Mass (g)",
    y = "Bill Depth (mm)",
    color = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Python Visualization

```{python python-analysis, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, error=TRUE}
# Import libraries
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Access the penguins data from R
penguins = r.py_penguins

# Create scatter plot with Python
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=penguins,
    x="body_mass_g",
    y="bill_depth_mm",
    hue="species",
    palette={"Adelie": "darkorange", "Chinstrap": "purple", "Gentoo": "#008080"},
    alpha=0.8,
    s=80
)

plt.title("Bill Depth vs Body Mass by Penguin Species (Python)")
plt.xlabel("Body Mass (g)")
plt.ylabel("Bill Depth (mm)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Julia Visualization

```{julia julia-analysis, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, eval=exists("julia_available") && julia_available, error=TRUE}
try
    # Basic Julia plot - only runs if Julia is available
    using CSV
    using DataFrames
    using Plots
    
    # Force the GR backend and set output format
    ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"  # Ensure headless plotting works
    Plots.gr()  # Explicitly use GR backend
    
    # Check if file exists
    if isfile("penguins_clean.csv")
        # Read data and create scatter plot
        penguins = CSV.read("penguins_clean.csv", DataFrame)
        
        # Convert species to string type
        penguins.species = string.(penguins.species)
        
        # Create scatter plot with hex color codes and store in variable
        plt = scatter(
            penguins.body_mass_g,
            penguins.bill_depth_mm,
            group=penguins.species,
            markersize=6,
            alpha=0.8,
            markerstrokewidth=0,
            color=["#FFA500", "#800080", "#008080"],  # hex codes for orange, purple, teal
            xlabel="Body Mass (g)",
            ylabel="Bill Depth (mm)",
            title="Bill Depth vs Body Mass by Penguin Species (Julia)",
            legend=:bottomright,
            size=(800, 500),
            dpi=300,
            fmt=:png  # Force PNG output format
        )
        
        # Explicitly display the plot
        display(plt)
        
        # Return the plot as the last expression
        plt
    else
        println("Error: penguins_clean.csv file not found")
        # Create a simple error plot
        plot(title="Error: Data file not found", legend=false)
    end
catch e
    println("Julia error: ", e)
    # Return something that can be displayed
    plot(title="Julia Error Occurred", legend=false)
end
```
